description:
In mfront/META_LEMA_ANI.mfront lines 151-158, the AXISYMMETRICAL and 3-D branches assign the Hill coefficient array differently, and the NORMAL components are self-consistent: AXIS uses axes (r,z,theta) with normals {MRR, MZZ, MTT}, 3-D uses (r,theta,z) with normals {MRR, MTT, MZZ}. Correct for each branch's own axis ordering.

The SHEAR triples, however, are exactly each other's: AXIS assigns {MRT, MRZ, MTZ} and 3-D assigns {MRZ, MRT, MTZ}. Swapping axes 2 and 3 between the branches should swap the first two shear slots too, so each branch appears to carry the other's shear ordering. That is the signature of a copy-paste transposition rather than a convention.

NOT SETTLED, and here is exactly why. Whether this is a defect depends on TFEL's hillTensor<N,real>(F,G,H,L,M,N) argument-to-shear-slot convention. Classical Hill pairs L with yz, M with zx, N with xy; if TFEL instead pairs L with xy the analysis changes from 'swapped' to 'cyclically rotated'. TFEL is a separate project and its headers are not present in this container (no Hill.hxx anywhere on the filesystem, no /usr/include/TFEL). Obtaining TFEL, or an authoritative statement of hillTensor's convention, is what closes this.

The metallurgy port reproduces the upstream ordering verbatim in HillAnisotropy::from_aster_3d, and names its struct fields by tensor slot so a caller can bypass the ambiguity. Do not 'fix' this without settling the convention first.
